newsitem.title: GERMANY: Iberia holds ex-Germany rates stable.
newsitem.headline: Iberia holds ex-Germany rates stable.

text.p: Iberia said it would hold its ex-Germany cargo rates stable this spring.
The airline's Germany sales manager, George von Doehren, said both demand and capacity for Latin American destinations, its main product for Germany, were rising.
"We changed our rates in September and see no reason to change them at present. There will be no change," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Carriers such as Martinair, Cargolux and Lan Chile were all increasing Europe to Latin America flights, he pointed out.

As GSA for Viasa in Germany, Iberia had been hit by the closure of the Venezuelan airline's three times a week DC-10 flights from Caracas to Frankfurt in early February with up to 15 tonnes capacity per flight, he said.
"We had a lot of freight for Caracas and the aircraft had good load factors," he said.
"We have certainly lost clients because they were companies who wanted to go directly to Caracas," he added.
Iberia now sold Caracas, which had been marked by ups and downs, as a transshipment destination through Madrid. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
